description: Formal risk acceptance register. Every deviation from policy or operating rules requires a signed risk acceptance from Skip Snow recorded here. Referenced by GOV-007 (Engineering Rules Are Standards), v4-004 (Operating Modes), and v4-006 (Deploy Authority).

entries.title: Competitor trademark usage in investor materials
entries.description: Business architecture investor document includes branded text representations of Yelp, ZocDoc, Healthgrades, and Angi in the competitive landscape section. These are trademark-protected brand names and visual identities.
entries.risk: Trademark holders may object to their brand being used in a competitive positioning document without permission.
entries.claude_warning: Claude advised that actual logos could not be used due to copyright. Boss overruled: 'Yes you can. Let them sue me. I accept the risk.'
entries.rationale: The competitive landscape section requires naming incumbents by name to make the positioning credible for investors. Fair use in comparative context.
entries.mitigation: Text-based brand representations only (no actual logo files). Used in private investor materials, not public marketing.

entries.title: AI classification of specialty prescriber and homeopathic status
entries.description: GPT-4.1-mini classifies each NUCC specialty code as can_prescribe (yes/no) and homeopathic (yes/no). This is a GOV-011 exception — the AI is making a classification decision, not just translating user input. The classification is cached per specialty code and used to filter the FindCare specialty list.
entries.risk: AI may misclassify edge-case specialties. A wrong classification could hide relevant providers or show irrelevant ones.
entries.claude_warning: Claude flagged GOV-011 violation — AI is deciding, not the system. Boss authorized: the classification is cached, auditable, and correctable.
entries.rationale: The alternative is hardcoding 800+ specialty classifications manually, which is error-prone and unmaintainable. GPT-4.1-mini classification is faster, covers all specialties, and the cached result can be reviewed and corrected. The risk is low — misclassification of a specialty is a filter error, not a clinical error.
entries.mitigation: Cache result in MongoDB. Human-reviewable. Corrections override AI classification. Log which specialties were AI-classified vs manually corrected.

entries.title: kill_zombies.py --kill-name exception for rogue processes
entries.description: DR-009 prohibits direct taskkill/kill from bash. kill_zombies.py only kills by port. A rogue pipeline process (not bound to a port) cannot be killed by the sanctioned tool. Boss authorized adding --kill-name flag to kill by process name.
entries.risk: Broader kill capability could accidentally terminate legitimate processes if wrong name is passed.
entries.rationale: Claude started a pipeline locally (v4-001C violation) that ran for 7+ hours. The governance guard now prevents this from happening again, but the orphan process must be killable. The guard blocks direct taskkill — kill_zombies.py is the only sanctioned path.
entries.mitigation: kill_zombies.py is the only way to kill. Guard blocks direct taskkill. --kill-name requires explicit process name argument. Cannot kill by wildcard.

entries.title: End-to-end governance commit architecture implementation
entries.description: Claude authorized to implement full governance commit architecture: create pydantic commit scan class, wire pre-commit hook to pydantic object, update chathealthy_devops_boot.py proxy, edit pipeline files to fix scan violations, update settings.json hooks, create/update bug records.
entries.risk: Low. Changes are to governance infrastructure, not product code. All changes traceable through this risk acceptance.
entries.rationale: Required to automate governance. Without this, Claude cannot be governed during commits and must escalate every scan violation manually.
entries.mitigation: Every change references RISK-004. Pre-commit scan validates. Boss reviews commit.

entries.title: Boot script rewrite — governance hook architecture
entries.description: Claude authorized to rewrite chathealthy_devops_boot.py: remove 25 check functions, replace with matrix scan per event, wire 7 Claude Code lifecycle hooks, add resume/directive/gotcha detection, GPT-4.1-mini for user_prompt_submit governance, regex for pre_tool_use gating. Fail open on crash.
entries.risk: Boot script changes could freeze hooks or block Claude if buggy. Mitigated by fail-open pattern and piped JSON testing before wiring live.
entries.rationale: Current boot silently crashes (NameError on undefined 'method' variable). No governance actually runs. Must fix to govern Claude.
entries.mitigation: Fail open on crash. Test all 7 events via piped JSON before wiring live. Don't touch project-level settings.json or brain JSONs. Prior gotchas documented and avoided.

entries.title: Deploy local to dev with mTLS security — unattended
entries.description: Claude authorized to: (1) Wire mTLS between FindCare and EvaluateCare locally and on HF, (2) Add nonce to session tokens, (3) Deploy to dev HF spaces, (4) Create dev smoke test. All state changes necessary to replicate local functionality on dev with proper security.
entries.risk: Low. Local is working and tested. Dev deployment is a copy with different bindings.
entries.rationale: Need to move forward. Local is a good base. Security must be in place for dev.
entries.mitigation: Smoke test validates dev after deploy. Ripcord: HF spaces can be paused/restarted.

entries.title: Dev database operations without pipeline certification
entries.description: Boss authorizes Claude to perform database operations (create indexes, drop collections, load data) on the dev frontend and pipeline clusters. Pipeline is not yet certified. Risk is negligible — dev environment, no production impact.
entries.risk: Dev data corruption or index misconfiguration. No production impact.
entries.rationale: Pipeline not yet certified. Manual operations needed to test FindCare. Dev environment is disposable.
entries.scope: dev environment only. Frontend and pipeline clusters.

entries.title: Lab database — create/destroy any DB object for testing
entries.description: Claude is authorized to create or destroy any database object (collections, indexes, documents) in any cluster in a Lab database. If the lab database does not exist, Claude may create it. Lab is for pytest execution only — never production data.
entries.risk: Accidental creation of lab artifacts on wrong cluster. No production impact — lab is isolated.
entries.rationale: Pytests need real database operations (GOV-006). Lab database is disposable test infrastructure.
entries.scope: Any cluster, lab database only. No other databases.

entries.title: Emergency test data — break engineering rules to get embeddings
entries.description: Boss authorizes Claude to break multiple engineering rules for up to 3 hours to produce test data with embeddings on the dev frontend cluster. This includes direct database writes, skipping pipeline, manual embedding generation, copying between environments, and any other operations needed to get FindCare specialty select working with real data.
entries.risk: High. Data may be inconsistent, pipeline state may diverge from database state, embeddings may not match pipeline-generated ones.
entries.rationale: No embeddings in any environment. Specialty select is broken. Cannot test without data. Pipeline has not delivered embeddings. Time-boxed emergency.
entries.scope: dev and qa frontend cluster. All collections in dev_PublicHealthData and qa_PublicHealthData.
